API reference

The operations Blowhorn defines, with their request fields and responses.

Blowhorn is used through its command-line interface and its MCP server. These are the operations behind them, listed with the fields each one takes and returns.

Not an HTTP API

Blowhorn ships a command-line interface and an MCP server today. It does not run an HTTP REST listener, so there is no server URL to send these requests to.

Actions

POST /cli/accept Accept pending LinkedIn connection invitations other people have sent you, one at a time with a randomized pause between each. An invitation LinkedIn flags with its "Take care when connecting" warning is dismissed and skipped, never accepted, and the run carries on; accepts and skips are reported separately, by name. Ignoring or declining an invitation is out of scope - this command only accepts.

Accept pending LinkedIn connection invitations other people have sent you, one at a time with a randomized pause between each. An invitation LinkedIn flags with its "Take care when connecting" warning is dismissed and skipped, never accepted, and the run carries on; accepts and skips are reported separately, by name. Ignoring or declining an invitation is out of scope - this command only accepts.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn accept`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Accept pending LinkedIn connection invitations other people have sent you, one at a time with a randomized pause between each. An invitation LinkedIn flags with its "Take care when connecting" warning is dismissed and skipped, never accepted, and the run carries on; accepts and skips are reported separately, by name. NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
ignore_risk boolean

Run this once even if your Risk Profile would hold it (a daily cap, quiet hours, outreach turned off or a pause after a sign-in challenge). Only this run; your Risk Profile stays as it is. A limit the platform itself publishes still applies

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output

Default: false
limit integer

Maximum acceptances confirmed in one run. A click is not an acceptance: only an invitation confirmed gone from the received list counts, and an invitation skipped because LinkedIn warned about it never consumes the budget. 0 means no limit (the run stops at the examination ceiling).

Default: 20
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Pace of the random delays between 'blowhorn accept' actions (page loads, typing, clicks, API calls): a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Platform scope for 'blowhorn accept'. One of: linkedin, all ('all' means every platform listed here)
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Risk Profile this run uses: cautious, standard or brisk. For this one run it beats the schedule's value, the profile's choice and configuration. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

What `blowhorn accept --json` prints on exit 0: the received invitations the run examined as profile URLs, how many it accepted, and how many it skipped. A row never carries a display name: identity is the profile URL only, so no person's name lands in a committed artifact. A flagged invitation ("Take care when connecting") is skipped, never confirmed: the warning's own confirm control is never clicked. On a dry run `sent` is 0 and `candidates` are the rows a real run would accept; the preview cannot know which invitation would raise the warning, because LinkedIn raises it only after Accept is clicked, so a dry run lists every candidate and says so rather than promising none would be skipped.

Response 200 of Accept pending LinkedIn connection invitations other people have sent you, one at a time with a randomized pause between each. An invitation LinkedIn flags with its "Take care when connecting" warning is dismissed and skipped, never accepted, and the run carries on; accepts and skips are reported separately, by name. Ignoring or declining an invitation is out of scope - this command only accepts. fields
NameTypeDescription
accepted integer

Invitations confirmed accepted, the same count as `sent`.
candidates required array of object

The received invitations the run examined, as profile URLs, in list order.
candidates[].profile_url required string (uri)

The inviter's LinkedIn profile URL. Never a display name.
dry_run required boolean

True when nothing was clicked and nothing was written.
examined integer

Rows examined, including rows left unanswered.
failed integer

Rows whose acceptance failed after the control was clicked.
held required array of object

Rows held as clicked with the outcome not read. Acceptance records none of its own; the list is empty unless a held row was carried in.
held[].profile_url required string (uri)
sent required integer

Invitations confirmed accepted. Always 0 on a dry run.
skipped required integer

Rows examined and left unanswered (flagged, stuck, unactionable, unidentifiable, or unreadable).
unconfirmed integer

Rows clicked whose acceptance could not be confirmed from the list.

default

POST /cli/follow Follow accounts on X, Bluesky, or GitHub. --limit 0 is target-only mode: the --target handle itself is followed and nothing else. With a positive --limit, --target is only the seed - the run follows up to --limit accounts drawn from that account's follower graph, and never follows the target. GitHub runs over the REST API with no browser, so its --dry-run performs the real follower walk and names exactly who would be followed.

POST /cli/post Publish pending posts or amplify existing content across supported platforms. GitHub is the one platform 'blowhorn post' cannot publish to: it is amplify-only, so '--platform github' needs an issue or pull-request URL (from --amplify or a github activity's 'Amplify' column) and refuses without one. That amplification adds all five uplifting reactions -- +1, laugh, hooray, heart, rocket -- to the target from every selected profile under its own GH_TOKEN, over the REST API with no browser, and re-running it adds none of them twice. With --payload-stdin it is a dry fire instead: one order that is not saved, read on stdin, is walked through the same dry run as far as the platform's final click, and nothing is posted or written to your Blowhorn account.

GitHub is the one platform 'blowhorn post' cannot publish to: it is amplify-only, so '--platform github' needs an issue or pull-request URL (from --amplify or a github activity's 'Amplify' column) and refuses without one. That amplification adds all five uplifting reactions -- +1, laugh, hooray, heart, rocket -- to the target from every selected profile under its own GH_TOKEN, over the REST API with no browser, and re-running it adds none of them twice. With --payload-stdin it is a dry fire instead: one order that is not saved, read on stdin, is walked through the same dry run as far as the platform's final click, and nothing is posted or written to your Blowhorn account. fields
NameTypeDescription
amplify string

URL of existing content to amplify instead of publishing something new. Overrides the activity's 'Amplify' column for this run. LinkedIn repost, X retweet/quote, Reddit upvote, Bluesky repost, GitHub reactions. On GitHub it names an issue or pull request and blowhorn adds all five uplifting reactions to it (+1, laugh, hooray, heart, rocket) from every selected profile under that profile's own GH_TOKEN; re-running adds none of them twice. --platform github REQUIRES a target -- this flag, or a github activity's 'Amplify' column -- because it amplifies only and cannot publish a new GitHub post; it refuses the run rather than doing nothing. Ignored for Slack -- use --target instead; Slack's 'Amplify' column selects the channel/DM/thread target, not an amplified source. Ignored for blog platforms (layer5/meshery).
check_queue boolean

Show pending posts from the content queue without publishing anything. Honors --platform / --profile / --exclude for filtering. Read-only - does not open a browser, hit a platform API, or invoke 'claude' for blog activities.

Default: false
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
ignore_risk boolean

Run this once even if your Risk Profile would hold it (a daily cap, quiet hours, outreach turned off or a pause after a sign-in challenge). Only this run; your Risk Profile stays as it is. A limit the platform itself publishes still applies

Default: false
json_output boolean

With --payload-stdin, end with the dry fire's result as one JSON object

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
message string

Send this text as one ad-hoc Slack message instead of posting from the content queue: no activity is read or marked done. Needs --platform slack, one profile named with --profile (not all, not a list) and --target ('#channel', '@user', a Slack channel link, or a Slack message link for a thread reply -- anything else is refused, never sent to #general); a profile from .blowhorn.yaml or BLOWHORN_PROFILE does not count as named. A link also picks the workspace's credentials. Refused with --check-queue or --amplify. --dry-run says what would be sent and sends nothing.
pace string

Pace of the random delays between 'blowhorn post' actions (page loads, typing, clicks, API calls): a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
payload_stdin boolean

Dry fire one order that is not saved: read one content item's values as JSON on stdin (the fields 'content upsert' takes, naming one Profile and one Platform) and walk it through the dry run as far as the platform's final click, printing each stage as it is reached. Needs --dry-run; --profile and --platform are not read. Writes nothing - no content item, schedule, ledger entry or run record. Hacker News is refused, because its dry run signs in.

Default: false
platform string

Platform scope for 'blowhorn post'. One of: bluesky, github, hn, layer5, linkedin, meshery, reddit, slack, x, all ('all' means every platform listed here)
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Risk Profile this run uses: cautious, standard or brisk. For this one run it beats the schedule's value, the profile's choice and configuration. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
slack_auth string

Which Slack credential may send, for one run: 'session' (your captured signed-in web session; the message is yours, with no app attached), 'user-token' (an xoxp- app token for you) or 'bot-token' (an xoxb- bot token), or a comma-delimited list of them tried in order (e.g. 'session,user-token,bot-token'). One value is directive: that credential or a refusal naming why. A token may show the Slack app's attribution. This flag, then BLOWHORN_SLACK_AUTH, then defaults.slack.auth_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, then the built-in, selects it; any other value is refused before anything runs. Dry runs and results name the credential that ran and whether it was a fallback
target string

Ad-hoc target that overrides the activity's values for this run. Slack: '#channel', '@user', a Slack channel link, or a Slack message link (posts as a thread reply); a link also picks that workspace's credentials. Other platforms: generally leave unset and use the activity's 'Comment on' column for replies. Ignored for blog platforms (layer5/meshery).
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

200

What a dry fire did: `post --dry-run --payload-stdin --json` read one order that is not saved (one content item's values, naming one profile and one platform) and walked it through the dry run as far as the platform's final click. `stages` lists each point the walk reached, in order, as it printed them. Nothing was posted and nothing was written to the store - no content item, schedule, ledger entry or run record. `post --json` reports nothing else: a queue run prints text. A refusal (Hacker News, a profile without the credential, a sign-in that failed) is the failure response, with the stages it reached.

POST /cli/source Collect people into the store from GitHub or LFX. GitHub lists one audience of one or more repositories (stargazers unless you name another) and stores one row per login. LFX reads one mentorship project's mentee list and upserts the mentees roster. One run names one platform: --repo and --audience belong to GitHub, --project and --start-page belong to LFX. A GitHub run lists the audience with the profile's stored GH_TOKEN. --dry-run lists that audience and writes nothing. Addresses are not printed. An LFX dry run names the list and writes nothing; a real LFX run reads each profile through Chrome. It does not follow, connect, or send mail.

POST /cli/star Star GitHub repositories. From every selected profile, over the REST API with no browser: --platform github --repo owner/repo, repeatable. Already-starred repositories are counted apart, never re-credited. --dry-run reads each repository's star state for real and names exactly which would be starred, issuing no PUT. A live run exits 0 only when at least one repository was confirmed and every attempted repository was confirmed by at least one profile. Star cannot be scheduled: it stars only the repositories named on the command line.

What `blowhorn withdraw --json` prints on exit 0: the sent invitations the run examined as profile URLs, how many withdrawals it confirmed, and how many cards it left alone. A row never carries a display name: identity is the profile URL only, so no person's name lands in a committed artifact. `--limit` is spent only on confirmed withdrawals: a click that reads no confirmation neither consumes the budget nor counts as withdrawn, and a combined unconfirmed/failed streak halts the run. POST /cli/profile/accounts List, map or unmap a profile's social accounts. An account is a Blowhorn

List, map or unmap a profile's social accounts. An account is a Blowhorn connection on one platform; a profile acts through the accounts mapped to it, one per platform, whoever owns them, so a person may keep several profiles and a brand profile reaches the accounts mapped to it. --map replaces the profile's account on that platform; --unmap leaves the connection itself intact. --page records the account's own page on the account already mapped for that platform, which is where the profile's handle is read from: Chrome profile discovery finds a sign-in, never a LinkedIn /in/ name.

POST /cli/profile/auth Refresh authentication/session state for one or more platforms.

Refresh authentication/session state for one or more platforms.

Supported platforms and authentication mechanisms:

linkedin - Persistent browser session. Automated login via LI_USERNAME / LI_PASSWORD in the store, with fallback to manual browser entry.

x - Persistent browser session. Automated login via X_USERNAME / X_PASSWORD in the store, with fallback to manual browser entry.

reddit - Persistent browser session. Automated login via RDDT_USERNAME / RDDT_PASSWORD in the store, with fallback to manual browser entry.

slack - Hybrid: session credentials (xoxc token + d cookie) captured through the run's browser driver (the extension by default), saved to the profile's Slack credential in the store, and reused for direct API calls. No Slack app install required. Use --workspace <host> to capture a new workspace; omit it to refresh every workspace listed under 'slack_workspaces' in that credential. Use --mode paste for the legacy OAuth-token flow.

bluesky - No browser. Logs in to Bluesky with a handle and app password -- the same login every post makes -- and stores the pair only when Bluesky accepts it, so a refused credential is never saved. For one named profile in a terminal it asks for both (the stored handle is the default; a blank app password keeps the stored one); --handle and --app-password-stdin supply them without a prompt. Otherwise the stored pair is logged in with and nothing is written.

Use --profile all to refresh every profile in your organization after applying any --exclude filters. The profiles are read from the store; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3.

With --headless the browser still opens, as a background window (Chrome is never run headless); only automated credential login is attempted and the manual browser fallback is skipped.

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn profile auth`, one property per parameter.

POST /cli/profile/create Create a profile in your organization on Blowhorn.

Create a profile in your organization on Blowhorn. It reads a JSON document on stdin (--payload-stdin) holding the fields a person sets: name (required), description and userId. userId is the organization member the profile represents, as `blowhorn org members` lists them; leave it out for a brand. Blowhorn adds the organization, and you own the profile. The name must be handle-shaped (lowercase letters, digits, '-' or '_') and not one another profile uses. Any other key is refused, every refusal comes before anything is sent, and --dry-run makes the same checks and sends nothing. No folder is created and no email is looked up.

Request body required

The JSON document `profile create --payload-stdin` and `profile update --payload-stdin` read: the v1beta3 `ProfilePayload` fields a person sets. Blowhorn adds `organizationId`; `owner` and `metadata` are never taken from this document. Any other key is refused. On an update the document is the whole of these fields: a `description` left out is cleared and a `userId` left out makes the profile a brand.

Request body of Create a profile in your organization on Blowhorn. fields
NameTypeDescription
description string

What the profile is for. Blank is the same as left out.
name required string

The profile's name, handle-shaped: lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters, never `all`, and not a name another visible profile uses. Trimmed and lowercased before it is checked.
userId string (uuid) | null

The member of the organization the profile represents, as `org members` lists them. Null or left out for a brand.

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

What `profile create --payload-stdin` did: the person-set fields it sent (or, with --dry-run, would send) to `createProfile`, and the profile Blowhorn answered with. `profile` is null on a dry run, which sends nothing.

ok required any
payload required object

The document after it was trimmed and normalized; a blank description or userId is left out.

payload.userId string

default

POST /cli/profile/set Store KEY=VALUE pairs on a profile: its platform credentials and its run settings.

Store KEY=VALUE pairs on a profile: its platform credentials and its run settings. A platform key (LI_*, X_*, RDDT_*, HN_*, SLACK_*, BLUESKY_*, GH_*, YT_*, IG_*, FB_*, TIKTOK_*, slack_workspaces and the <WORKSPACE>_SLACK_* session keys) is stored in that platform's credential in the store, where runs read it. A run setting (Risk Profile, Risk Profile By Platform, Daily Caps, Quiet Hours, Quiet Hours Time Zone) is stored in the profile's settings in your Blowhorn account, and a value a run could not read is refused. A blank value clears a key. Any other key is refused, and every refusal comes before anything is sent. Nothing is written to a file. The output names the keys that changed and never echoes a value. Replacing a credential an API check judges (GH_TOKEN, the Bluesky handle or app password, a Slack token or captured session) sets that platform back to not checked in profile status until the next check, because each such check records which credential it judged. A browser platform's check is about its saved session and stays.

A profile is created with profile create, and who it represents changes with profile update.

POST /cli/profile/status Report what each profile in your organization is set up for: the platforms it holds

Report what each profile in your organization is set up for: the platforms it holds an account for (credential key names only -- values are never printed), the browser session directory and its last-modified time, whether another blowhorn process holds its lock, the last recorded session check, and whether the profile is excluded by default. The profiles are your organization's list in your Blowhorn account, read once; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3. No browser and no platform network by default: accounts are read from the store's credentials, once for every profile, with the person each profile represents. A credential read the store fails leaves every account unknown and is named on a Credentials: line, not fatal, and a check made then skips every platform and keeps its last results. With --json each platform also carries account_status: the status of the profile's account in your Blowhorn account (connected, disconnected, ...), read once for every profile, or null when none is mapped.

--check-sessions runs a read-only probe per configured platform (LinkedIn, X and Reddit open the saved session in a background window and look for the signed-in page; GitHub, Bluesky and Slack call their APIs) and records the result in the profile's session_status.json under data/cache/profiles/, and records a LinkedIn, X or Reddit sign-in it finds (or one that ended) on the profile's account in your Blowhorn account. It never logs in, never types a credential, and reports 'busy' instead of waiting when a session is in use. --check-platform runs that same probe for one platform only and leaves every other platform's recorded result alone; --check-platform github checks the profile's GitHub token in the store against GitHub (the login it signs in as, its scopes and what they lack) with no browser at all. --roster additionally reads the profiles roster from the store to show which platforms each profile has a handle for; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3, and a roster that reads empty or cannot be read is reported on a Roster: line, not fatal. --chrome additionally reads this machine's Chrome profile mappings from the store, once, and Chrome's own profile list, and adds a Chrome column: the mapped Chrome profile directory and whether the name and account recorded when it was mapped still match (drift, missing, unknown). A mapping is identity, never permission. A Chrome profile list that cannot be read is reported on a Chrome: line, not fatal.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn profile status`, one property per parameter.

Run the --check-sessions probe for this one platform only (implies --check-sessions) and leave the other platforms' recorded results as they are. One of: linkedin, x, reddit, hn, slack, bluesky, github; github, bluesky and slack are API calls and open no browser. Unlike --platform it is never read from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform, so a default cannot narrow a check nobody asked to narrow

POST /cli/profile/switch Set a profile as the default profile in global config. The profile must be in your organization's list, read from the store; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3.

Set a profile as the default profile in global config. The profile must be in your organization's list, read from the store; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn profile switch`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Set a profile as the default profile in global config. The profile must be in your organization's list, read from the store; a store that cannot be reached is the named cause and exit 3. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
name required string

Profile name to set as default
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn profile switch' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Platform scope for 'blowhorn profile'. One of: bluesky, linkedin, reddit, slack, x, all ('all' means every platform listed here)
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn profile switch' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

POST /cli/profile/update Replace the fields a person sets on one profile.

Replace the fields a person sets on one profile. The profile is named by its name or its id, and the fields come from the JSON document on stdin (--payload-stdin): name (required), description and userId. The document is the whole of them: a description left out is cleared, and a userId left out makes the profile a brand that represents nobody. The profile's run settings (Risk Profile, caps, quiet hours) are read just before the write and sent back as they are, and its owner is unchanged. The same refusals as `profile create` apply, a rename onto another profile's name included; --dry-run sends nothing.

Request body required

The JSON document `profile create --payload-stdin` and `profile update --payload-stdin` read: the v1beta3 `ProfilePayload` fields a person sets. Blowhorn adds `organizationId`; `owner` and `metadata` are never taken from this document. Any other key is refused. On an update the document is the whole of these fields: a `description` left out is cleared and a `userId` left out makes the profile a brand.

Request body of Replace the fields a person sets on one profile. fields
NameTypeDescription
description string

What the profile is for. Blank is the same as left out.
name required string

The profile's name, handle-shaped: lowercase letters, digits, `-` or `_`, starting with a letter or digit, at most 64 characters, never `all`, and not a name another visible profile uses. Trimmed and lowercased before it is checked.
userId string (uuid) | null

The member of the organization the profile represents, as `org members` lists them. Null or left out for a brand.

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

What `profile update --payload-stdin` did: the person-set fields it sent (or, with --dry-run, would send) to `updateProfile`, and the profile Blowhorn answered with. `profile` is null on a dry run, which sends nothing.

Response 200 of Replace the fields a person sets on one profile. fields
NameTypeDescription
dry_run required boolean
ok required any
payload required object

The document after it was trimmed and normalized; a blank description or userId is left out.
payload.description string
payload.name required string
payload.userId string
profile required one of null, ProfileListItem

default

POST /cli/content/approve Approve one activity by number, so a post run may publish it, and record who approved it and when in the activity's 'Approved by' column. This is the person's door under approval mode (defaults.approval.mode): activities an agent queued wait here. Approving is a person's act, so a caller marked as an agent (BLOWHORN_ACTOR=agent) or without a terminal is refused in every mode. An activity that is already approved is refused. --dry-run reports the activity and approves nothing.

POST /cli/content/list List the content queue's activities with their state and, for each, the profiles a post run would select it for right now ('Pending for' -- the same selection 'blowhorn post --check-queue' prints, read from the profiles roster). One read of the store; nothing is written and no browser opens.

List the content queue's activities with their state and, for each, the profiles a post run would select it for right now ('Pending for' -- the same selection 'blowhorn post --check-queue' prints, read from the profiles roster). One read of the store; nothing is written and no browser opens.

--profile keeps activities addressed to those profiles or to 'all'; --platform keeps one platform; --pending keeps only activities some profile would pick up now. --json is the shape the desktop app's Content screen reads, fingerprints included.

Request body of List the content queue's activities with their state and, for each, the profiles a post run would select it for right now ('Pending for' -- the same selection 'blowhorn post --check-queue' prints, read from the profiles roster). NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false

POST /cli/content/posts List the posts as one list: every post in the content queue with its own schedule inline (its 'Promote On', or not scheduled), then the schedule's jobs as rows of their own, labelled by their command. A job does not point at a post: a 'post' job drains the queue at run time, selecting by profile, platform, approval and 'Promote On', so the jobs are shown unlinked rather than joined to posts they do not name.

List the posts as one list: every post in the content queue with its own schedule inline (its 'Promote On', or not scheduled), then the schedule's jobs as rows of their own, labelled by their command. A job does not point at a post: a 'post' job drains the queue at run time, selecting by profile, platform, approval and 'Promote On', so the jobs are shown unlinked rather than joined to posts they do not name.

--profile and --platform filter both halves; --pending keeps only the posts some profile would pick up now (the jobs are not filtered by it). --json is the shape the desktop app's posts list reads, each post carrying its schedule and the jobs unlinked. One read of each half of the store; nothing is written and no browser opens.

Prints the one posts list: every post with its schedule inline (its own `Promote On`), then the schedule's jobs as unlinked rows in their `schedule list` shape. `ok` is false when either read reports missing columns.

Response 200 of List the posts as one list: every post in the content queue with its own schedule inline (its 'Promote On', or not scheduled), then the schedule's jobs as rows of their own, labelled by their command. A job does not point at a post: a 'post' job drains the queue at run time, selecting by profile, platform, approval and 'Promote On', so the jobs are shown unlinked rather than joined to posts they do not name. fields
NameTypeDescription
count required integer
extra_columns required array of string
generated_at required string

Local time, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.
job_count required integer
jobs required array of ScheduleActivity

The schedule's jobs, unlinked: no job names a post, because a `post` job selects its content at run time; each job is labelled by its own command.
jobs[].activity required integer
jobs[].command required string
jobs[].connection object | null

The activity's Google Chrome connection, from the tick's gate (#1600): null when a run may start. `held` is a run that waits, not one that fails, with the plain reason and the one in-app action that clears it; `heal` is a connection Blowhorn reconnects on its own before the run; `open` is a mapped Google Chrome profile that is not open, which Blowhorn opens in the background before the run. Absent from older engines.
jobs[].connection.action required string | null

The one thing the person can do: `turn_on_extension` (turn the Blowhorn extension on in that Google Chrome profile), `reconnect` (reconnect it now), `choose_chrome_profile` (choose or confirm the Google Chrome profile) or `restart_chrome` (restart Google Chrome, the one action left when a native host process from before an upgrade is still answering and ending it did not clear the hold); null when Blowhorn heals it alone.
jobs[].connection.chrome_directory required string | null

The Google Chrome profile directory the activity's profile is mapped to; null when none is.
jobs[].connection.profile required string
jobs[].connection.reason required string | null

Why it waits or reconnects, in plain words that name no command.
jobs[].connection.state required string

Values: held, heal, open
jobs[].driver_mode required string
jobs[].due required string

`yes` when the activity's time has come: it is enabled and valid, no machine holds a live claim on it, and its `next_run` has passed. Always `no` when `next_run` is empty. A paused activity still reads `yes`, and `paused` says the tick is holding it.

Values: yes, no
jobs[].enabled required string

Values: yes, no
jobs[].errors required string

Validation errors joined by a semicolon; empty when the activity is valid.
jobs[].held_here required boolean

The claim is this install's own: this macOS user on this computer. Never decided by the hostname alone, which every macOS user on a Mac shares.
jobs[].last_error required string
jobs[].last_log_path required string
jobs[].last_run_at required string
jobs[].lock_stale required boolean
jobs[].locked required boolean
jobs[].locked_at required string
jobs[].locked_by required string
jobs[].max_retries required integer

The retry budget for each arming; see `Max Retries` in the activity's values.
jobs[].next_run required string

When the tick next takes the activity, in local time. Empty when it never will: a completed once-only activity, or a completed or failed activity with no Next Run At. Never the activity's old Run At.
jobs[].params required ScheduleParams

The parsed Params of a schedule activity, keyed by the command's own parameter names. A value is a string, a number or a boolean as the activity's text parses.
jobs[].pause_reason required string
jobs[].paused required string

Values: yes, no
jobs[].paused_at required string
jobs[].paused_by required string
jobs[].platform required string

The platform, or `all`.
jobs[].profile required string

The profile, or a hyphen when the activity names none.
jobs[].quiet_hours required string

`yes` when the activity is inside its quiet hours now (see `quiet_hours_window`): the tick holds it, unclaimed, and runs it when the window ends. Computed, never stored.

Values: yes, no
jobs[].quiet_hours_tz required string

The zone `quiet_hours_window` is read in: an IANA name, or this computer's zone; empty when no window is set.
jobs[].quiet_hours_until required string

When the current window ends, in local time; empty when the activity is not in quiet hours now.
jobs[].quiet_hours_window required string

The quiet-hours window in force for the activity's profile, `HH:MM-HH:MM` like `22:00-07:00`; empty when no window is set anywhere for it.
jobs[].recurrence required string
jobs[].retry_count required integer

Failed attempts since the activity was last armed; see `Retry Count` in the activity's values.
jobs[].retry_delay_minutes required integer
jobs[].risk_hold required string

Why a Run now would be held, including while the profile is warming up. Empty when the activity may run. A confirmation passes this hold except when `risk_hold_source` is `published`.
jobs[].risk_hold_source required string

Where the hold comes from. `published` is a limit the platform states, which a confirmation does not pass. Empty when `risk_hold` is empty.
jobs[].risk_profile required string

The preset the activity resolves to, from the tick's gate; empty for an activity without one profile and one platform, which names no single preset.
jobs[].risk_profile_effective required string

What the tick enforces: cautious while warming, whatever was chosen; empty with `risk_profile`.
jobs[].risk_profile_source required string

The layer that chose the preset (`schedule` when the activity's own value did, `builtin` when nothing chose one); empty with `risk_profile`.
jobs[].risk_profile_warming required string

`yes` while the profile or this computer is warming up; empty with `risk_profile` (an activity on every platform names no single preset).

Values: yes, no,

jobs[].run_at required string
jobs[].status required string

The activity's stored status, such as pending, scheduled, running, retrying or failed. Never a lock.
missing_columns required array of string

Schedule columns the store is missing, as `schedule list` reports them.

ok required boolean

jobs[].connection.action required string | null

The one thing the person can do: `turn_on_extension` (turn the Blowhorn extension on in that Google Chrome profile), `reconnect` (reconnect it now), `choose_chrome_profile` (choose or confirm the Google Chrome profile) or `restart_chrome` (restart Google Chrome, the one action left when a native host process from before an upgrade is still answering and ending it did not clear the hold); null when Blowhorn heals it alone.
jobs[].connection.chrome_directory required string | null

The Google Chrome profile directory the activity's profile is mapped to; null when none is.
jobs[].connection.profile required string
jobs[].connection.reason required string | null

Why it waits or reconnects, in plain words that name no command.
jobs[].connection.state required string

Values: held, heal, open
jobs[].driver_mode required string
jobs[].due required string

`yes` when the activity's time has come: it is enabled and valid, no machine holds a live claim on it, and its `next_run` has passed. Always `no` when `next_run` is empty. A paused activity still reads `yes`, and `paused` says the tick is holding it.

Values: yes, no
jobs[].enabled required string

Values: yes, no
jobs[].errors required string

Validation errors joined by a semicolon; empty when the activity is valid.
jobs[].held_here required boolean

The claim is this install's own: this macOS user on this computer. Never decided by the hostname alone, which every macOS user on a Mac shares.
jobs[].last_error required string
jobs[].last_log_path required string
jobs[].last_run_at required string
jobs[].lock_stale required boolean
jobs[].locked required boolean
jobs[].locked_at required string
jobs[].locked_by required string
jobs[].max_retries required integer

The retry budget for each arming; see `Max Retries` in the activity's values.
jobs[].next_run required string

When the tick next takes the activity, in local time. Empty when it never will: a completed once-only activity, or a completed or failed activity with no Next Run At. Never the activity's old Run At.
jobs[].params required ScheduleParams

The parsed Params of a schedule activity, keyed by the command's own parameter names. A value is a string, a number or a boolean as the activity's text parses.
jobs[].pause_reason required string
jobs[].paused required string

Values: yes, no
jobs[].paused_at required string
jobs[].paused_by required string
jobs[].platform required string

The platform, or `all`.
jobs[].profile required string

The profile, or a hyphen when the activity names none.
jobs[].quiet_hours required string

`yes` when the activity is inside its quiet hours now (see `quiet_hours_window`): the tick holds it, unclaimed, and runs it when the window ends. Computed, never stored.

Values: yes, no
jobs[].quiet_hours_tz required string

The zone `quiet_hours_window` is read in: an IANA name, or this computer's zone; empty when no window is set.
jobs[].quiet_hours_until required string

When the current window ends, in local time; empty when the activity is not in quiet hours now.
jobs[].quiet_hours_window required string

The quiet-hours window in force for the activity's profile, `HH:MM-HH:MM` like `22:00-07:00`; empty when no window is set anywhere for it.
jobs[].recurrence required string
jobs[].retry_count required integer

Failed attempts since the activity was last armed; see `Retry Count` in the activity's values.
jobs[].retry_delay_minutes required integer
jobs[].risk_hold required string

Why a Run now would be held, including while the profile is warming up. Empty when the activity may run. A confirmation passes this hold except when `risk_hold_source` is `published`.
jobs[].risk_hold_source required string

Where the hold comes from. `published` is a limit the platform states, which a confirmation does not pass. Empty when `risk_hold` is empty.
jobs[].risk_profile required string

The preset the activity resolves to, from the tick's gate; empty for an activity without one profile and one platform, which names no single preset.
jobs[].risk_profile_effective required string

What the tick enforces: cautious while warming, whatever was chosen; empty with `risk_profile`.
jobs[].risk_profile_source required string

The layer that chose the preset (`schedule` when the activity's own value did, `builtin` when nothing chose one); empty with `risk_profile`.
jobs[].risk_profile_warming required string

`yes` while the profile or this computer is warming up; empty with `risk_profile` (an activity on every platform names no single preset).

Values: yes, no,

POST /cli/content/upsert Create a post, or update one in place, from a JSON object of column: value pairs in the queue's own column names. Without --activity a new activity is created and given the next activity number; with --activity the payload is merged over that activity, and every column it does not name is left as it was.

Create a post, or update one in place, from a JSON object of column: value pairs in the queue's own column names. Without --activity a new activity is created and given the next activity number; with --activity the payload is merged over that activity, and every column it does not name is left as it was.

Platform must be one 'blowhorn post' publishes to (linkedin, x, reddit, slack, bluesky, github, layer5, meshery); Approved? takes yes or no (JSON true/false are written as yes/no); Promote On must parse (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS); Profile must name a profile the store knows, or 'all'. Unknown fields are refused rather than written. --expected-fingerprint refuses the write if the activity changed since 'content get' or 'content list' read it. --dry-run prints the payload and touches nothing.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn content upsert`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Create a post, or update one in place, from a JSON object of column: value pairs in the queue's own column names. Without --activity a new activity is created and given the next activity number; with --activity the payload is merged over that activity, and every column it does not name is left as it was. fields
NameTypeDescription
activity integer

Activity number to update in place; omit to create a new activity
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
expected_fingerprint string

Refuse the write if the post's fingerprint (from 'content get' or 'content list') no longer matches
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output (the shape the desktop app's Content screen reads)

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn content upsert' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
payload required string

JSON object of Content column: value pairs in the queue's own column names, for example '{"Platform":"x","Profile":"company","Message Text":"hello","Approved?":"yes"}'
platform string

Platform filter for 'blowhorn content': 'content list' keeps the activities whose Platform column names this platform, and no other content subcommand reads it. One of: bluesky, github, hn, layer5, lfx, linkedin, meshery, reddit, slack, x, all ('all' applies no filter, so every activity is listed)

Default: "all"
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)

Default: "all"
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn content upsert' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

POST /cli/schedule/destinations List the post destinations that belong to an organization rather than to a person -- the organization blogs today -- and whether this organization has each one: a destination is set up when at least one of its profiles is opted in to it (a platform opt-in in the store, the same fact 'blowhorn post' reads to decide who may publish there). A destination no profile is opted in to can never be posted to, so the desktop app offers no new activity for it; activities already saved for it still show and run. Reads the store once; writes nothing.

POST /cli/schedule/fleet List every computer sharing your schedule whose background service has reported lately, and whether each is on duty, read from the last scheduler pass it recorded in the store: a pass that ran says on duty, a paused one says off duty, and one that failed says last pass failed. A computer with no pass in the reporting window (about half an hour) is left out, because nothing recent says what it is doing. Reads only -- it claims nothing and changes nothing.

NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Prints one schedule activity with its column values, fingerprint, parsed params, next scheduled time, lock state, validation errors, the Risk Profile it resolves to, and the limits the platform publishes on its action. It carries no `ok` key.

NameTypeDescription
activity required integer
fingerprint required string

A hash of the values, to pass back as the expected fingerprint of an update.
lock_stale required boolean
locked required boolean
params required ScheduleParams

The parsed Params of a schedule activity, keyed by the command's own parameter names. A value is a string, a number or a boolean as the activity's text parses.
published_limits required array of PublishedLimit

The limits the platform publishes on this activity's action, each naming the presets that would go past it. Empty without one profile and one platform, or where the platform publishes none.
published_limits[].above required array of string

The presets whose cap for this activity's profile, once warm, would go past this limit and is cut to it. Empty when every preset stays within it.
published_limits[].actions required array of string

The gate actions the one count covers; several when the platform counts them together.
published_limits[].as_of required string

The date the page was read.
published_limits[].count required integer
published_limits[].label required string

The provenance label of the reading (`UNVERIFIED - docs`).
published_limits[].per required string

Values: hour, day
published_limits[].platform required string
published_limits[].platform_label required string

The platform's display name (`X`, `Bluesky`).
published_limits[].source required string

The platform's page the limit was read from.
published_limits[].what required string

The platform's own unit in plain words (`follows`, `original posts`).
risk_profile required string

The preset the activity resolves to, from the tick's gate; empty without one profile and one platform.
risk_profile_effective required string

What the tick enforces: cautious while warming, whatever was chosen.
risk_profile_source required string

The layer that chose the preset (`schedule` when the activity's own value did).
risk_profile_warming required string

Values: yes, no
scheduled_for required string

The same instant `schedule list` prints as `next_run`: when the tick next takes the activity, in local time. Empty when it never will: a completed once-only activity, or a completed or failed activity with no Next Run At. Never the activity's old Run At.
validation_errors required array of string
values required ScheduleValues

A schedule row's columns, each a string (empty when unset): the command and its params as `key=value;key=value`, when it runs and how it repeats, its retry budget, its status and the lock a running machine holds.
values.Command required string
values.Driver Mode required string
values.Enabled required string
values.Last Error required string
values.Last Log Path required string
values.Last Run At required string
values.Locked At required string
values.Locked By required string
values.Max Retries required string

The retry budget for each arming: how many times a failed run is retried before the row is failed. Raising it alone does not schedule a failed row again.
values.Next Run At required string

When the row is next due, in local time. Empty on a completed or failed row means never due again. An update that gives a completed or failed row a Next Run At, or changes its Run At, schedules it again in the same write: Status scheduled and Retry Count 0, with Last Run At, Last Error and Last Log Path kept, unless the update sets Status itself.
values.Params required string
values.Platform required string
values.Profile required string
values.Recurrence required string
values.Retry Count required string

Failed attempts since the row was last armed. A success sets it to 0, and so does an update that schedules a completed or failed row again.
values.Retry Delay Minutes required string
values.Risk Profile required string

The activity's own Risk Profile (#1009): `cautious`, `standard` or `brisk`, or empty to inherit the preset its profile and platform resolve to.
values.Run At required string
values.Status required string

default

POST /cli/schedule/list List scheduled actions and whether they are currently due. With several machines sharing the store the Locked By column names the holder and marks this machine's own claims; a paused action reads paused: yes beside its due state, because due keeps meaning its time has passed.

NameTypeDescription
activities required array of ScheduleActivity
activities[].activity required integer
activities[].command required string
activities[].connection object | null

The activity's Google Chrome connection, from the tick's gate (#1600): null when a run may start. `held` is a run that waits, not one that fails, with the plain reason and the one in-app action that clears it; `heal` is a connection Blowhorn reconnects on its own before the run; `open` is a mapped Google Chrome profile that is not open, which Blowhorn opens in the background before the run. Absent from older engines.
activities[].connection.action required string | null

The one thing the person can do: `turn_on_extension` (turn the Blowhorn extension on in that Google Chrome profile), `reconnect` (reconnect it now), `choose_chrome_profile` (choose or confirm the Google Chrome profile) or `restart_chrome` (restart Google Chrome, the one action left when a native host process from before an upgrade is still answering and ending it did not clear the hold); null when Blowhorn heals it alone.
activities[].connection.chrome_directory required string | null

The Google Chrome profile directory the activity's profile is mapped to; null when none is.
activities[].connection.profile required string
activities[].connection.reason required string | null

Why it waits or reconnects, in plain words that name no command.
activities[].connection.state required string

Values: held, heal, open
activities[].driver_mode required string
activities[].due required string

`yes` when the activity's time has come: it is enabled and valid, no machine holds a live claim on it, and its `next_run` has passed. Always `no` when `next_run` is empty. A paused activity still reads `yes`, and `paused` says the tick is holding it.

Values: yes, no
activities[].enabled required string

Values: yes, no
activities[].errors required string

Validation errors joined by a semicolon; empty when the activity is valid.
activities[].held_here required boolean

The claim is this install's own: this macOS user on this computer. Never decided by the hostname alone, which every macOS user on a Mac shares.
activities[].last_error required string
activities[].last_log_path required string
activities[].last_run_at required string
activities[].lock_stale required boolean
activities[].locked required boolean
activities[].locked_at required string
activities[].locked_by required string
activities[].max_retries required integer

The retry budget for each arming; see `Max Retries` in the activity's values.
activities[].next_run required string

When the tick next takes the activity, in local time. Empty when it never will: a completed once-only activity, or a completed or failed activity with no Next Run At. Never the activity's old Run At.
activities[].params required ScheduleParams

The parsed Params of a schedule activity, keyed by the command's own parameter names. A value is a string, a number or a boolean as the activity's text parses.
activities[].pause_reason required string
activities[].paused required string

POST /cli/schedule/pause Pause all scheduled processing: every tick keeps running but claims no activities until 'blowhorn schedule resume', and due times carry forward. A job already running finishes first. Pausing has three scopes and an activity is claimed only when none of them says paused: without a flag it is this machine only (a local file, never the store), --all is every machine sharing the store, and --activity N is one scheduled activity on every machine.

Pause all scheduled processing: every tick keeps running but claims no activities until 'blowhorn schedule resume', and due times carry forward. A job already running finishes first. Pausing has three scopes and an activity is claimed only when none of them says paused: without a flag it is this machine only (a local file, never the store), --all is every machine sharing the store, and --activity N is one scheduled activity on every machine.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn schedule pause`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Pause all scheduled processing: every tick keeps running but claims no activities until 'blowhorn schedule resume', and due times carry forward. A job already running finishes first. Pausing has three scopes and an activity is claimed only when none of them says paused: without a flag it is this machine only (a local file, never the store), --all is every machine sharing the store, and --activity N is one scheduled activity on every machine. fields
NameTypeDescription
activity integer

Pause one scheduled activity instead of a whole machine: that job is claimed by nobody until 'blowhorn schedule resume --activity N', and every other activity keeps running everywhere. Distinct from setting the activity's Enabled to no, which is an editorial state with no reason and no intent to resume
all_machines boolean

Pause every machine sharing this store, not just this one: no machine claims an activity until 'blowhorn schedule resume --all'. Recorded in the store with who paused it and why, so every machine reports the same reason. Without this flag the pause is this machine only

Default: false
by string

Tool name recorded as the pause owner, as <tool>@<host> (default: cli)
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn schedule pause' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Platform filter for 'blowhorn schedule': it selects which scheduled activities this command reads or acts on, and is not a platform blowhorn posts to directly. One of: bluesky, github, hn, layer5, lfx, linkedin, meshery, reddit, slack, x, all ('all' applies no filter, so every scheduled activity is included)

Default: "all"
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)

Default: "all"
reason string

Short note stored with the pause and shown by 'blowhorn schedule status'
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn schedule pause' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

POST /cli/schedule/tick Run one scheduler polling pass against due scheduled actions, executing each through the same command routing the CLI uses and writing a per-job log under <log-dir>/scheduler/. While 'blowhorn schedule pause' is in effect the pass claims nothing unless --ignore-pause is passed; a real pass also records its heartbeat in <log-dir>/scheduler/last-tick.json and appends one tick record to the run ledger, <log-dir>/runs/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl. Browser visibility comes from each job: its own headless=/headed= params, then the environment, then Settings.

Run one scheduler polling pass against due scheduled actions, executing each through the same command routing the CLI uses and writing a per-job log under <log-dir>/scheduler/. While 'blowhorn schedule pause' is in effect the pass claims nothing unless --ignore-pause is passed; a real pass also records its heartbeat in <log-dir>/scheduler/last-tick.json and appends one tick record to the run ledger, <log-dir>/runs/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl. Browser visibility comes from each job: its own headless=/headed= params, then the environment, then Settings.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn schedule tick`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Run one scheduler polling pass against due scheduled actions, executing each through the same command routing the CLI uses and writing a per-job log under <log-dir>/scheduler/. While 'blowhorn schedule pause' is in effect the pass claims nothing unless --ignore-pause is passed; a real pass also records its heartbeat in <log-dir>/scheduler/last-tick.json and appends one tick record to the run ledger, <log-dir>/runs/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl. Browser visibility comes from each job: its own headless=/headed= params, then the environment, then Settings. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
ignore_pause boolean

Run even while 'blowhorn schedule pause' is in effect; without it a paused scheduler claims nothing

Default: false
ignore_quiet_hours boolean

Run even inside the quiet hours (defaults.quiet_hours, or a profile's own Quiet Hours setting); without it a due activity inside the window is held until it ends

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output

Default: false
limit integer

Maximum number of due activities to process; 0 means no limit

Default: 0
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Pace handed to every action 'blowhorn schedule tick' runs in-process this pass -- the random delays between that action's browser or API steps: a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Platform filter for 'blowhorn schedule': it selects which scheduled activities this command reads or acts on, and is not a platform blowhorn posts to directly. One of: bluesky, github, hn, layer5, lfx, linkedin, meshery, reddit, slack, x, all ('all' applies no filter, so every scheduled activity is included)

Default: "all"
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)

Default: "all"
risk_profile string

Risk Profile this run uses: cautious, standard or brisk. For this one run it beats the schedule's value, the profile's choice and configuration. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

What schedule tick prints with --json: the pass's counts and one entry per activity it handled (or would handle with --dry-run).

Response 200 of Run one scheduler polling pass against due scheduled actions, executing each through the same command routing the CLI uses and writing a per-job log under <log-dir>/scheduler/. While 'blowhorn schedule pause' is in effect the pass claims nothing unless --ignore-pause is passed; a real pass also records its heartbeat in <log-dir>/scheduler/last-tick.json and appends one tick record to the run ledger, <log-dir>/runs/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl. Browser visibility comes from each job: its own headless=/headed= params, then the environment, then Settings. fields
NameTypeDescription
cancelled required boolean
candidates required integer
checked required integer
heartbeat_path required string | null
missing_columns required array of string
ok required boolean

False when the schedule is missing required columns, or when this install is already running a tick.
pause required object | null

The pause that held the pass, with its scope (machine, all or activity); null when not paused.
paused required boolean
processed required integer
record_path required string | null
refused required string | null

The sentence Blowhorn prints when this install is already running a tick. The command then exits 1. Null on a pass that ran.
results required array of object

One entry per activity the pass handled. Entries always carry activity, command, profile and status; a pass adds further keys for some statuses.
results[].activity required integer
results[].command required string
results[].profile required string
results[].reason string

Why a preview blocked the activity, in words. Set when status is blocked, and on a reclaim skip.
results[].status required string

For example would-run, blocked, held, invalid, done, failed or cancelled.
skipped_cancelled required array
skipped_paused required array

Due activities left waiting because of a pause.
stop required one of StopState, null

The organization-wide stop in force, or null.
stopped required boolean

True when the organization-wide stop ended the pass at a safe point; a stopped pass is also cancelled, with the stop named in `stop`.
store_error required string | null

Set on a degraded pass when the store was unreachable (the command then exits 3).
store_unavailable_since required string | null
store_unavailable_ticks required integer

default
