POST /cli/auth/logout Sign out of Blowhorn and clear the local entitlement attestation cache.

Sign out of Blowhorn and clear the local entitlement attestation cache.

Removes the token 'blowhorn auth login' saved (Keychain item ai.blowhorn.cloud-token), the account it wrote to cloud.yaml (organization_id, display_name and the account facts), the process cache and the Keychain attestation item (ai.blowhorn.entitlement.v2). POST /cli/auth/status Show whether Blowhorn credentials and an entitlement attestation are present.

Show whether Blowhorn credentials and an entitlement attestation are present.

Reports token configured (never the token value), organization id, api_base, enforcement mode (BLOWHORN_ENTITLEMENT), and a summary of the last Feature read. Live, it first re-reads the signed-in account from Blowhorn (name, photo, organizations, plan) into cloud.yaml and follows the organization your Blowhorn session in the browser has selected; BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION still wins when set, and the plan read and shown is that organization's. --offline answers from presence checks only: it reads no saved secret, so macOS shows no Keychain prompt, and it makes no network request (the desktop app runs it at launch). Exits 3 when this computer is not signed in: no token, a token Blowhorn refused, or Blowhorn could not be reached. --offline exits 3 only when no token is configured.

Response 200 of Show whether Blowhorn credentials and an entitlement attestation are present. fields
NameTypeDescription
account required object | null

Who is signed in, for the desktop app's account button and menu. Read from cloud.yaml, where sign-in caches it and a live auth status refreshes it from Blowhorn's own answers, each checked against the meshery/schemas construct Blowhorn consumes (schemas/meshery/consumed.yaml): User and its Preference from GET /api/identity/users/profile, AvailableOrganization from GET /api/identity/orgs, and the organization's Subscription and its Plan from /api/entitlement. So --offline answers it with no secret read and no request. Null when no token is configured. A field Blowhorn did not answer is null. The organization is the one organization_id names: the session's active organization (Preference.selectedOrganizationId when the account is still a member, else the first listed, the same choice the browser session makes), unless BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION names another.
account.avatar_url required string | null

User.avatarUrl (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user), the profile photo in your Blowhorn account.
account.email required string | null

User.email (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user).
account.first_name required string | null

User.firstName (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user).
account.last_name required string | null

User.lastName (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user).
account.organization_count required integer | null

How many live organizations the account belongs to, as GET /api/identity/orgs last counted them; more than one offers Switch organization.
account.organization_name required string | null

AvailableOrganization.name (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization) of the organization this status reports.
account.organizations required array of object

The account's live organizations (GET /api/identity/orgs, soft-deleted ones left out, up to Blowhorn's page of 100), in Blowhorn's order; Switch organization offers these.
account.organizations[].description required string | null

AvailableOrganization.description (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization), null when Cloud gave none; shown on hover beside the id to tell two organizations of the same name apart.
account.organizations[].id required string

AvailableOrganization.id (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization).
account.organizations[].name required string | null

AvailableOrganization.name (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization).
account.plan_name required string | null

Plan.name (meshery/schemas v1beta3 plan, the PlanName enum) of the organization this status reports, exactly as Blowhorn names it, and Free when Blowhorn answered with no current subscription (every organization is on Free unless one names another plan). Null only when it has never been read for that organization; the app then shows the organization alone.

Values: Free, Team Designer, Team Operator, Enterprise,

api_base required string | null
attestation required object | null

The cached plan attestation, or null when none has been read.

attestation.features required object

attestation.features.max_devices_per_seat required integer | null

Null means unlimited.

attestation.features.scheduler required boolean

ISO 8601 UTC instant the plan was fetched.
attestation.fresh required boolean
attestation.organization_id required string | null
attestation_present required boolean

Whether a saved plan is held. With --offline, from the Keychain item's attributes only; live, whether attestation is non-null.
checked required string

presence for --offline (attributes only: no secret read, no request); live when the saved plan was read and, when due, refreshed from Blowhorn.

Values: presence, live
cloud_yaml required string | null

Path of the cloud.yaml in use, if any.
display_name required string | null
enforcement required string

The entitlement enforcement mode, or "invalid (<reason>)" when the setting does not parse.
fetch_error required string | null
ok required boolean

False when this computer is not signed in. True when a token is configured and, live, Blowhorn accepted it.
organization_id required string | null
permission_keys array of string

Live only: the ids of the permission keys the signed-in session holds in the Blowhorn parent organization (GET /api/identity/orgs/by-domain resolves the parent organization, then GET /api/identity/orgs/{id}/users/keys), which the desktop app's Diagnostics gate matches the Access Diagnostics key id against. Empty when no token is configured or when either read fails: the gate fails closed. Absent from the --offline payload, which makes no request.
previous_account required object | null

Who was signed in on this computer before the session ended, for the desktop app's returning sign-in screen, which greets that person by name. Read from cloud.yaml, where sign-out removes the account: a name still there with no token configured means the token was lost, removed or has timed out, never that the person signed out. Only the name and email, never the photo or the organizations. Null while a token is configured (account answers then), after a sign-out, and when cloud.yaml names nobody. Answered by --offline too: no secret read, no request.

Why this computer is not signed in, present only when signed_in is false. no token means none is configured. token refused means Blowhorn answered 401 or 403. unreachable means Blowhorn could not be reached. --offline reports only no token.

Values: no token, token refused, unreachable

POST /cli/auth/switch-organization Switch the signed-in account to another of its organizations.

Switch the signed-in account to another of its organizations.

Makes ORGANIZATION_ID the organization the account's Blowhorn session has selected, with the same write Blowhorn's and Meshery's own organization switchers send (PUT /api/identity/users/preferences, selectedOrganizationId), so the browser and this computer follow it. ORGANIZATION_ID must be one of the account's organizations ('auth status --json' lists them as account.organizations). Then reports what 'auth status' reports, read live for the new organization. BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION, when set, still names the organization this computer reports. --dry-run checks the id and sends nothing.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn auth switch-organization`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Switch the signed-in account to another of its organizations. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
organization_id required string

The id of one of the account's organizations (auth status --json: account.organizations).
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn auth switch-organization' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn auth': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn auth switch-organization' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

What auth status reports, read live after the account's selected organization was switched in Blowhorn (or, with --dry-run, read offline with nothing sent). BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION, when set, still names the organization this computer reports.

Response 200 of Switch the signed-in account to another of its organizations. fields
NameTypeDescription
account required object | null

Who is signed in, for the desktop app's account button and menu. Read from cloud.yaml, where sign-in caches it and a live auth status refreshes it from Blowhorn's own answers, each checked against the meshery/schemas construct Blowhorn consumes (schemas/meshery/consumed.yaml): User and its Preference from GET /api/identity/users/profile, AvailableOrganization from GET /api/identity/orgs, and the organization's Subscription and its Plan from /api/entitlement. So --offline answers it with no secret read and no request. Null when no token is configured. A field Blowhorn did not answer is null. The organization is the one organization_id names: the session's active organization (Preference.selectedOrganizationId when the account is still a member, else the first listed, the same choice the browser session makes), unless BLOWHORN_CLOUD_ORGANIZATION names another.
account.avatar_url required string | null

User.avatarUrl (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user), the profile photo in your Blowhorn account.

User.firstName (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user).
account.last_name required string | null

User.lastName (meshery/schemas v1beta2 user).
account.organization_count required integer | null

How many live organizations the account belongs to, as GET /api/identity/orgs last counted them; more than one offers Switch organization.
account.organization_name required string | null

AvailableOrganization.name (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization) of the organization this status reports.
account.organizations required array of object

The account's live organizations (GET /api/identity/orgs, soft-deleted ones left out, up to Blowhorn's page of 100), in Blowhorn's order; Switch organization offers these.
account.organizations[].description required string | null

AvailableOrganization.description (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization), null when Cloud gave none; shown on hover beside the id to tell two organizations of the same name apart.
account.organizations[].id required string

AvailableOrganization.id (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization).
account.organizations[].name required string | null

AvailableOrganization.name (meshery/schemas v1beta2 organization).
account.plan_name required string | null

Plan.name (meshery/schemas v1beta3 plan, the PlanName enum) of the organization this status reports, exactly as Blowhorn names it, and Free when Blowhorn answered with no current subscription (every organization is on Free unless one names another plan). Null only when it has never been read for that organization; the app then shows the organization alone.

False when this computer is not signed in. True when a token is configured and, live, Blowhorn accepted it.
organization_id required string | null
permission_keys array of string

Live only: the ids of the permission keys the signed-in session holds in the Blowhorn parent organization (GET /api/identity/orgs/by-domain resolves the parent organization, then GET /api/identity/orgs/{id}/users/keys), which the desktop app's Diagnostics gate matches the Access Diagnostics key id against. Empty when no token is configured or when either read fails: the gate fails closed. Absent from the --offline payload, which makes no request.
previous_account required object | null

Who was signed in on this computer before the session ended, for the desktop app's returning sign-in screen, which greets that person by name. Read from cloud.yaml, where sign-out removes the account: a name still there with no token configured means the token was lost, removed or has timed out, never that the person signed out. Only the name and email, never the photo or the organizations. Null while a token is configured (account answers then), after a sign-out, and when cloud.yaml names nobody. Answered by --offline too: no secret read, no request.

sign_in_problem string

Values: no token, token refused, unreachable

Whether this computer is signed in to Blowhorn.

pace string

Pace of the one random wait 'blowhorn slack delete' takes: before each confirmed delete after the first when --profile names several profiles (a single profile, or a dry run, never waits): a preset name (fast/normal/slow) or a numeric multiplier (e.g. 0.5, 2.0). Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

risk_profile string

Risk Profile this run uses: cautious, standard or brisk. For this one run it beats the schedule's value, the profile's choice and configuration. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
slack_auth string

Which Slack credential may send, for one run: 'session' (your captured signed-in web session; the message is yours, with no app attached), 'user-token' (an xoxp- app token for you) or 'bot-token' (an xoxb- bot token), or a comma-delimited list of them tried in order (e.g. 'session,user-token,bot-token'). One value is directive: that credential or a refusal naming why. A token may show the Slack app's attribution. This flag, then BLOWHORN_SLACK_AUTH, then defaults.slack.auth_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, then the built-in, selects it; any other value is refused before anything runs. Dry runs and results name the credential that ran and whether it was a fallback
target string

The message: a Slack message link, or its ts with --channel and --workspace
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false
workspace string

The workspace host (e.g. mesheryio.slack.com) when --target does not name one; for whoami, which workspace to ask

POST /cli/slack/edit Replace the text of a Slack message this profile sent with 'blowhorn slack send' (chat.update). Only your own messages: the store's send ledger must show this profile sent that ts, or the result is not_sent_by_profile before any Slack call. A dry run unless --confirm. --target is the message link (its own ts, never the ?thread_ts= parent) or a bare ts with --channel and --workspace; the text comes from --message, --file or stdin ('-') and is sent untouched. Several profiles (--profile a,b) run one after another. Exit codes as 'slack send'.

List every profile's captured Slack workspaces (or only the --profile names given), the credentials each holds (session, user-token, bot-token) and which one --slack-auth would use. Reads the store and makes no Slack call. No secret is printed.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn slack profiles`, one property per parameter.

Request body of List every profile's captured Slack workspaces (or only the --profile names given), the credentials each holds (session, user-token, bot-token) and which one --slack-auth would use. Reads the store and makes no Slack call. No secret is printed. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Print the result as JSON (no secrets)

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn slack profiles' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn slack': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn slack profiles' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
slack_auth string

Which Slack credential may send, for one run: 'session' (your captured signed-in web session; the message is yours, with no app attached), 'user-token' (an xoxp- app token for you) or 'bot-token' (an xoxb- bot token), or a comma-delimited list of them tried in order (e.g. 'session,user-token,bot-token'). One value is directive: that credential or a refusal naming why. A token may show the Slack app's attribution. This flag, then BLOWHORN_SLACK_AUTH, then defaults.slack.auth_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, then the built-in, selects it; any other value is refused before anything runs. Dry runs and results name the credential that ran and whether it was a fallback
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

POST /cli/slack/send Send one message to Slack as one profile, or as each of several (--profile a,b: one after another, each with its own idempotency key, ledger entry and result; one profile's failure never stops the next, and exit is 0 only when every profile succeeded), exactly once. A dry run unless --confirm: the dry run resolves the credential, the target and the idempotency key and says what would happen. --target takes a message link (a thread reply: the ?thread_ts= parent when the link is a reply's), a channel link (a top-level post), or #channel, @user or a channel id with --workspace. The text comes from --message, --file <path>, or stdin with --message - or --file -, and is sent untouched (Slack mrkdwn included). Every send carries a client_msg_id and is claimed in the store's send ledger under its idempotency key (--idempotency-key, else derived from profile, workspace, channel, thread and text) before it goes out: a key already sent replays its ts and link without sending again, and a send whose answer was never recorded is 'outcome unknown' and is never resent automatically. The result names the credential that ran (--slack-auth), whether that was a fallback, warns when a token may show a Slack app's attribution, and reports bot_id, app_id, bot_profile or subtype on Slack's answer. Exit codes: 0 sent, replayed or previewed; 1 refused (credential or Slack); 2 usage or key conflict; 3 store unavailable or a contended key; 4 outcome unknown; 5 rate-limited (Retry-After kept).

Send one message to Slack as one profile, or as each of several (--profile a,b: one after another, each with its own idempotency key, ledger entry and result; one profile's failure never stops the next, and exit is 0 only when every profile succeeded), exactly once. Ask Slack (auth.test) who a profile's Slack credential is in one workspace: user, user id and team, with the credential --slack-auth allowed and whether that was a fallback. Sends no message. --workspace may be left out when the profile has captured exactly one workspace.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn slack whoami`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Ask Slack (auth.test) who a profile's Slack credential is in one workspace: user, user id and team, with the credential --slack-auth allowed and whether that was a fallback. Sends no message. --workspace may be left out when the profile has captured exactly one workspace. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Print the result as JSON (no secrets)

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn slack whoami' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn slack': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn slack whoami' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
slack_auth string

Which Slack credential may send, for one run: 'session' (your captured signed-in web session; the message is yours, with no app attached), 'user-token' (an xoxp- app token for you) or 'bot-token' (an xoxb- bot token), or a comma-delimited list of them tried in order (e.g. 'session,user-token,bot-token'). One value is directive: that credential or a refusal naming why. A token may show the Slack app's attribution. This flag, then BLOWHORN_SLACK_AUTH, then defaults.slack.auth_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, then the built-in, selects it; any other value is refused before anything runs. Dry runs and results name the credential that ran and whether it was a fallback
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false
workspace string

The workspace host (e.g. mesheryio.slack.com) when --target does not name one; for whoami, which workspace to ask

Start the installed background service, or ask a running one for a pass now.

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn service start`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Start the installed background service, or ask a running one for a pass now. fields
NameTypeDescription
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false

profile string

POST /cli/store Report whether this computer can use Blowhorn, and say why not when it cannot: signed in, a client the server still accepts, and a member of the organization. --replay-spool also drains the results already waiting in the local write-back spool; apart from it, nothing here writes anything.

Report whether this computer can use Blowhorn, and say why not when it cannot: signed in, a client the server still accepts, and a member of the organization. --replay-spool also drains the results already waiting in the local write-back spool; apart from it, nothing here writes anything.

Exits 0 when the store is usable and 3 when it is not -- the same code every other command uses for an unreachable store, so a wrapper can tell an outage from a failed job. --json emits the check as one object: ok, exitCode, cause, error, organization, reachable, spoolDepth, warnings, rungs, replay and cloud; configured is always true, and configPath, configMode, dsn, tunnel, serverVersion, schema and validation are always null.

Write out the results waiting in the local write-back spool now, rather than leaving them for the next run to drain, and report how many write-backs were pushed, kept and dropped. With --dry-run it writes nothing and reports what the run without it would have done

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

Prints the Blowhorn check: the capabilities handshake as one rung, a replay rung with `--replay-spool`, and any warnings. One shape covers a usable store (`ok: true`, exit 0) and a named cause (`ok: false`, exit 3), so the desktop's Setup row reads both alike. The keys the retired Postgres probe filled (`configPath`, `configMode`, `dsn`, `tunnel`, `serverVersion`, `schema`) are always null and `properties` is always empty.

Analytics

POST /cli/analytics/activities Print several activities' results at once, from one set of store reads: the same result 'analytics activity' prints for each (delivery, reception where it is collected, and the derived follower change, per profile and platform), in the order given. An activity number the queue does not have is listed as not found rather than failing the rest. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3.

Print several activities' results at once, from one set of store reads: the same result 'analytics activity' prints for each (delivery, reception where it is collected, and the derived follower change, per profile and platform), in the order given. An activity number the queue does not have is listed as not found rather than failing the rest. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3.

Request body required

The flags and arguments of `blowhorn analytics activities`, one property per parameter.

Request body of Print several activities' results at once, from one set of store reads: the same result 'analytics activity' prints for each (delivery, reception where it is collected, and the derived follower change, per profile and platform), in the order given. An activity number the queue does not have is listed as not found rather than failing the rest. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3. fields
NameTypeDescription
activities required array of integer

Activity numbers, as 'content list' prints them
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit machine-readable JSON output

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn analytics activities' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Platform scope for 'blowhorn analytics'. One of: bluesky, linkedin, x, all ('all' means every platform listed here)

Default: "all"
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)

Default: "all"
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn analytics activities' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

Prints several activities' results from one set of store reads: one `AnalyticsActivityResponse` per activity found, in the order asked, and `missing`, the activity numbers (as strings, the way `activityId` spells them) the content queue does not have, in the order asked. A computer with no store prints the Problem shape and exits 3.

Response 200 of Print several activities' results at once, from one set of store reads: the same result 'analytics activity' prints for each (delivery, reception where it is collected, and the derived follower change, per profile and platform), in the order given. An activity number the queue does not have is listed as not found rather than failing the rest. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3. fields

POST /cli/analytics/activity Print one activity's result, read from the store: for each profile and platform it is addressed to, whether it went out (when, the live link, which computer and browser profile ran it, and on a failure the error and the fix), how it was received where reception is collected (LinkedIn page activities, from the page content exports, with the date the figures were read and a comparison with the page's typical activity), and the follower change around it, labelled derived. Anything not collected says so, with a reason, never as a zero. A computer with no store prints a short explanation and exits 3.

POST /cli/analytics/history Print the follower history the collectors have already recorded, as one dated series read from the store: every LinkedIn page and every profile's X trend, whichever machine collected them. Tolerates the N/A cells the collectors write, and derives the 30-day net, growth rate and (LinkedIn pages only) unfollowed figures, each labelled derived in the output; X profiles carry a net change and no unfollowed count, because X measures only the total. A store that cannot be reached exits 3.

Prints follower history read from the analytics CSVs: one series point per subject per date, a summary per subject with the 30-day derivations, and what each source file held. LinkedIn pages also carry `unfollowed_30d` and their reception: the latest impressions and reactions, the date they were read, and their derived 30-day change.

Response 200 of Print the follower history the collectors have already recorded, as one dated series read from the store: every LinkedIn page and every profile's X trend, whichever machine collected them. Tolerates the N/A cells the collectors write, and derives the 30-day net, growth rate and (LinkedIn pages only) unfollowed figures, each labelled derived in the output; X profiles carry a net change and no unfollowed count, because X measures only the total. A store that cannot be reached exits 3. fields

POST /cli/analytics/import-exports Read the LinkedIn page content exports already on disk and record each activity's reception figures in the store: impressions, views, clicks, click-through rate, likes, comments, reposts, follows and engagement rate from each export's All posts sheet, dated by the export. Each activity is matched to its activity by its link; activities made outside Blowhorn are kept and marked unmatched. Prints activities read, matched and stored per file. Safe to run again: a reading lands once per activity and export date. --dry-run reads and matches without writing.

chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)

POST /cli/analytics/operations Aggregate the run ledger, read from the store, into operations per profile, per platform, per command, per day or per host: how many runs each action made, what they confirmed, skipped and failed, and which profiles and platforms were active. Reads the ledger only - a dry run is counted apart and never as an operation, and records exist from the first run after this command shipped, so a window older than that reports zero rather than guessing. Per host is the per-machine history now that several machines share one store. A store that cannot be reached exits 3.

POST /cli/analytics/pages List, add, remove or seed the LinkedIn pages analytics collects from for the signed-in organization, read from and written to the store: each page's name, its kind (company or showcase) and its numeric page id, from which the followers and content analytics URLs are derived. Collection walks the enabled pages; an organization with none configured collects the pages in use before per-organization configuration, and 'seed' writes those pages into the store once so the organization can edit its own list from there. --dry-run shows an add, remove or seed without writing. A store that cannot be reached exits 3.

POST /cli/classify-url Say what a link is, by the platform rules the engine keeps: 'post' when it names an existing post or comment on a supported platform, with the verbs that platform takes ('respond', 'amplify'); 'page' for any other web link, with the platform whose site it is on; 'none' for anything that is not a web link. The desktop app's drop reads this to choose its sheet. It reads the link text only: it opens no browser, signs in to nothing and writes nothing.

POST /cli/setup Set up Blowhorn on this computer, safely and repeatably. Each step checks first and changes only what is missing or stale, so running it again is safe; every line says ok (already in place), changed (written by this run), planned, declined, todo (needs you) or failed. It checks that blowhorn is on PATH, lists your Chrome profiles from Chrome's Local State file, writes the Chrome extension's native-messaging host when it is missing or stale, adds the marked PATH block to your shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/fish/config.fish) when it is missing, so new terminals find blowhorn in ~/.local/bin, and checks your Blowhorn sign-in. Before it writes the native host it says, in plain language, which Chrome profiles the file reaches and asks; the PATH block is asked about the same way; --yes answers yes for a script, and --dry-run writes nothing. With --json, or with no terminal to ask in, nobody is asked: it writes nothing and reports planned. It never starts, opens or attaches to Chrome and installs no extension. It ends with what is left for you: sign in, install the extension from the Chrome Web Store, check it answers, and get the app from blowhorn.ai/download. --json prints the same as one object.

Response 200 of Set up Blowhorn on this computer, safely and repeatably. Each step checks first and changes only what is missing or stale, so running it again is safe; every line says ok (already in place), changed (written by this run), planned, declined, todo (needs you) or failed. It checks that blowhorn is on PATH, lists your Chrome profiles from Chrome's Local State file, writes the Chrome extension's native-messaging host when it is missing or stale, adds the marked PATH block to your shell startup files (~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc, ~/.config/fish/config.fish) when it is missing, so new terminals find blowhorn in ~/.local/bin, and checks your Blowhorn sign-in. Before it writes the native host it says, in plain language, which Chrome profiles the file reaches and asks; the PATH block is asked about the same way; --yes answers yes for a script, and --dry-run writes nothing. With --json, or with no terminal to ask in, nobody is asked: it writes nothing and reports planned. It never starts, opens or attaches to Chrome and installs no extension. It ends with what is left for you: sign in, install the extension from the Chrome Web Store, check it answers, and get the app from blowhorn.ai/download. --json prints the same as one object. fields

Names of the steps whose state is ok.
changed required array of string

Names of the steps whose state is changed.
next_steps required array of string
profiles required array of string

Chrome profiles detected, labelled by name and directory. These are real people's names; never commit real output.
steps required array of object
steps[].detail required string
steps[].name required string
steps[].state required string

Values: ok, changed, planned, declined, todo, failed

POST /cli/uninstall Remove Blowhorn from this machine: the background service (the ai.blowhorn.service LaunchAgent, booted out and its file removed), the Chrome native host (the com.blowhorn.chrome_extension manifest, its launcher under ~/Library/Application Support/Blowhorn, and the every-profile install entries 'chrome extension-install --all-profiles' wrote), the ~/.local/bin/blowhorn launcher tools/install.sh wrote (a launcher without the installer's marker is kept), the marked PATH block in ~/.zshrc, ~/.bashrc and ~/.config/fish/config.fish (only the block comes out; the rest of each file stays), /Applications/Blowhorn.app (the bundle first unregisters its own Login Items entries - open at login and the background service - through its --unregister-login-items; a bundle too old to have it is reported not unregistered, naming System Settings > General > Login Items as the step left to you), and the checkout's venv/ (--venv-dir, else BLOWHORN_VENV_DIR, else <checkout>/venv, removed only when it holds pyvenv.cfg), node_modules/, desktop/node_modules/ and data/logs/. Every item is reported as removed, not present, not checked, kept, not unregistered or failed, in that order; a failed or not-unregistered item is reported and the run goes on, exiting 1 at the end. The sign-in on this machine (the Keychain item, the account record, and the guided setup progress) is removed on every uninstall. Local data is kept and named -- the store connection file an older version wrote (no longer read), the desktop app's state, Blowhorn's own Chrome trees and the checkout's data/cache/ (each profile's runtime state) -- unless --purge is given, which removes it after you type 'purge' at the prompt (or pass --yes, which --json needs); your Blowhorn account is never touched. Nothing under a Chrome profile is read or written: nobody is signed out of Chrome, Google Chrome stays installed, and the extension stays on the Chrome Web Store. Refused by name, in a dry run too, while a scheduler tick, a service pass, an extension run, Blowhorn.app, a desktop app started from this checkout or, with --purge, a Chrome on ~/.blowhorn is running, and while a write-back spool this run removes (under the checkout's data/logs/, or the app's state under --purge) holds run records that have not reached the shared store (run 'blowhorn store --replay-spool' first, or pass --discard-unsynced-runs when the store will never be reachable again); a spool in any other log directory is left in place and named with its count. --dry-run lists every item and removes nothing. ./tools/uninstall.sh at the checkout root runs the same code with the system Python once the venv is gone. --from-trash is the run the app makes on itself after you drag it to the Trash, before the Trash is emptied: purge scope is forced, the bundle is looked for in ~/.Trash as well as /Applications and removing it takes it out of the Trash, and the Login Items entry of a bundle that is already gone is reported instead of failing the run. macOS only; Linux and any other platform are refused by name.

NameTypeDescription
bin_dir string

Where tools/install.sh wrote the launchers (its --bin-dir; default ~/.local/bin)
chrome_launch string

How this run reaches Google Chrome, for one run: 'extension' (the default) drives Chrome through the Blowhorn Chrome extension and starts no Playwright Chrome; 'persistent' launches Blowhorn's own Chrome from chrome.automation_data_dir with the mapped profile directory inside it; 'cdp' attaches to a running Chrome that is ready per 'blowhorn chrome status' (daily Chrome asks you to Allow once per connection; a dedicated attach-chrome started with 'blowhorn chrome attach-chrome start' does not); and 'auto' attaches when Chrome is ready and launches otherwise. This flag, then BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, then BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, then defaults.chrome.launch_mode in .blowhorn.yaml, selects the driver a run actually uses. Any other value is refused before anything runs. Every browser run needs the profile mapped with 'blowhorn chrome map' first, in any mode. A scheduler tick's jobs each resolve their own mode (this flag on the tick, BLOWHORN_CHROME_LAUNCH, the job's driver mode, BLOWHORN_BROWSER_DRIVER, defaults.chrome.launch_mode, then the extension)
config string

Path to global config file (default: ./.blowhorn.yaml)
discard_unsynced_runs boolean

Give up the run records waiting in a write-back spool this run removes (runs/pending-store.ndjson under the checkout's data/logs/, or the app's state under --purge) instead of refusing, when the shared store will never be reachable again; otherwise run 'blowhorn store --replay-spool' first. Asks you to type discard after naming the count of records it deletes (or pass --yes, which --json needs)

Default: false
dry_run boolean

Simulate execution without making changes

Default: false
exclude string

Profiles to exclude when using --profile all (comma delimited); alias: --e; use 'none' or an empty string to clear configured defaults
from_trash boolean

The run the app makes on itself after you drag Blowhorn.app to the Trash, before the Trash is emptied: purge scope is forced (everything goes, local data included), the bundle is looked for in ~/.Trash as well as /Applications, removing it takes it out of the Trash, and the Login Items entry of a bundle that is already gone is reported instead of failing the run. Asks you to type purge first (or pass --yes, which --json needs)

Default: false
headed boolean

Keep the browser window visible and in front (overrides --headless) so a person can finish a sign-in or challenge

Default: false
headless boolean

Run unattended in a background browser window: never headless (Chrome would announce the run as HeadlessChrome to every site) and no waiting for a person at a sign-in or challenge. When the run attaches to your running Chrome (--chrome-launch cdp, or auto while 'blowhorn chrome status' says ready) the tab opens in its own visible Chrome window instead: a hidden tab is throttled, so the previous app is only re-activated once

Default: false
json_output boolean

Emit the report as one JSON object: ok, dry_run, purge, from_trash, refusals, every item with its result, and the kept paths

Default: false
log_dir string

Directory where daily rotated stdout/stderr logs are persisted while still streaming to the console
pace string

Accepted by 'blowhorn uninstall' because --pace is a global flag, but this command does no paced work -- it sleeps between nothing -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs and appears only in the Pace column of the -v summary. Resolved as CLI flag, then BLOWHORN_PACE, then defaults.pace in .blowhorn.yaml (normal when none is set); an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
platform string

Accepted and ignored by 'blowhorn uninstall': this command never acts on a platform, so --platform has no effect here -- including a value inherited from BLOWHORN_PLATFORM or defaults.platform in .blowhorn.yaml
profile string

Profile context (name, comma-delimited names, or 'all' alias for all profiles)
purge boolean

Also remove local data a plain uninstall keeps: ~/.config/blowhorn (an older version's store.yaml, no longer read), the rest of ~/Library/Application Support/Blowhorn, ~/.blowhorn, the app's per-user Library state, the checkout's data/cache/ (each profile's runtime state) and the pause file. The sign-in (Keychain item and account record) is removed on every uninstall, with or without this flag. Asks you to type purge first; your Blowhorn account is never touched

Default: false
risk_profile string

Accepted by 'blowhorn uninstall' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
venv_dir string

The virtualenv tools/install.sh created (its --venv-dir; default BLOWHORN_VENV_DIR, else <checkout>/venv). Removed only when it holds pyvenv.cfg; the filesystem root, your home directory, the checkout and a directory holding either are refused
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false
yes boolean

Confirm --purge, --from-trash or --discard-unsynced-runs without the prompt, for a run with no terminal; refused without one of them

Default: false

POST /cli/upgrade Carry this Mac's local data from an earlier home into this one. It carries profiles, analytics history, every run-ledger line (duplicates included), the write-back spool, the pause and the settings you changed. The earlier home is left exactly as it was, nothing already in the new home is overwritten, and a file that differs is kept and named in the report. Browser session folders are never carried. The pause is carried first, so a paused Mac is paused in the new home even if a later part fails. Each completed carry is recorded in upgrades.json in the new home, so it runs once; a carry that fails is not recorded and the next run tries again, adding nothing twice. While a scheduled pass is still running from the earlier home the answer is busy and nothing is touched. The earlier home is found from --source, then from the engine record the app wrote before this launch, then from the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn. A folder that belongs to another macOS user is never carried, even when named with --source; the report says so and carries nothing. --dry-run -- including one that comes from your settings -- only plans: the answer is planned, nothing is written, and the upgrade is still due. The desktop app runs this itself at launch; you never need a terminal for it.

Accepted by 'blowhorn upgrade' because --risk-profile is a global flag, but this command does no gated work -- no Risk Profile hold, cap or pace applies to it -- so the value changes nothing about how it runs. A value after the command word wins over one before it; an unrecognized value is rejected before anything runs
source string

The earlier version's home to carry data from; without it the engine record from before this launch is read, then the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn
verbose boolean

Enable verbose output (includes COMMAND SUMMARY)

Default: false

Responses

200

What the command prints to stdout with --json when it exits 0.

The upgrade report: whether this Mac's local data was carried from an earlier version's home into the home this version uses, and what each step carried. The same shape is printed on a busy or failed run with ok false and error set (a busy or failed status is read from status, here and in details on the desktop runner's failure shape).

Response 200 of Carry this Mac's local data from an earlier home into this one. It carries profiles, analytics history, every run-ledger line (duplicates included), the write-back spool, the pause and the settings you changed. The earlier home is left exactly as it was, nothing already in the new home is overwritten, and a file that differs is kept and named in the report. Browser session folders are never carried. The pause is carried first, so a paused Mac is paused in the new home even if a later part fails. Each completed carry is recorded in upgrades.json in the new home, so it runs once; a carry that fails is not recorded and the next run tries again, adding nothing twice. While a scheduled pass is still running from the earlier home the answer is busy and nothing is touched. The earlier home is found from --source, then from the engine record the app wrote before this launch, then from the previous checkout at ~/code/blowhorn. A folder that belongs to another macOS user is never carried, even when named with --source; the report says so and carries nothing. --dry-run -- including one that comes from your settings -- only plans: the answer is planned, nothing is written, and the upgrade is still due. The desktop app runs this itself at launch; you never need a terminal for it. fields
